## System certificates

Some company networks send HTTPS traffic through a proxy. The proxy
signs the traffic again with the company’s own certificate. Python HTTP
clients trust only the certificates bundled in `certifi`. Behind such a
proxy, every hosted backend fails with a TLS handshake error. The error
does not mention the proxy.

[`use_system_certs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#use_system_certs)
makes Python’s `ssl` module trust the certificate store of the operating
system. The company certificate is in that store. The function imports
`truststore`. It returns `False` when that import fails. Urai calls the
function once on import. Set `URAI_SYSTEM_CERTS=0` to turn this off. The
older name `RISHI_SYSTEM_CERTS` is also read. Pass `force=True` to apply
the change regardless of that setting.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/core.py#L18"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### use_system_certs

``` python
def use_system_certs(
    force:bool=False
):
```

*Make Python trust the OS certificate store, returning False when
`truststore` is missing or `URAI_SYSTEM_CERTS=0`.*

``` python
os.environ['URAI_SYSTEM_CERTS'] = '0'
test_eq(use_system_certs(), False)
test_eq(use_system_certs(force=True), True)
del os.environ['URAI_SYSTEM_CERTS']
```

## Usage

[`UsageStats`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#usagestats)
records the tokens that one chat turn used. A local backend reports only
prompt tokens and completion tokens. Prompt tokens are the tokens sent
to the model. Completion tokens are the tokens the model generated. A
hosted provider can also report tokens read from its prompt cache,
tokens written to it, reasoning tokens, and the cost in dollars. A field
that the backend does not report stays at zero.

Two
[`UsageStats`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#usagestats)
values add field by field. The usage of a whole session is the `sum` of
its turns. Adding `None` returns the other value unchanged. The sum
keeps the `model` of the first value that names one. The cell below adds
two turns:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/core.py#L30"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### UsageStats

``` python
def UsageStats(
    prompt_tokens:int=0, # tokens in the prompt
    completion_tokens:int=0, # tokens the model generated
    total_tokens:int=0, # prompt + completion, as the backend reports it
    n:int=0, # turns folded into this total
    cached_tokens:int=0, # prompt tokens served from a KV or prefix cache
    cost:float=0.0, # what the provider charged; 0 for local inference
    model:NoneType=None, # which model spent them
    reasoning_tokens:int=0, # thinking tokens, which hosted providers bill separately
    cache_creation_tokens:int=0, # tokens written to the provider's prompt cache
):
```

*Token usage for one chat turn.*

``` python
a = UsageStats(prompt_tokens=10, completion_tokens=5, total_tokens=15, n=1, model='gpt-5.1')
b = UsageStats(prompt_tokens=3, completion_tokens=2, total_tokens=5, n=1)
tot = a + b
tot
```

    total=20|in=13|out=7|turns=2|model=gpt-5.1

``` python
test_eq((tot.prompt_tokens, tot.completion_tokens, tot.total_tokens, tot.n), (13, 7, 20, 2))
test_eq(tot.model, 'gpt-5.1')
test_eq(sum([a, b]).total_tokens, 20)   # `sum` starts at 0, which `__radd__` absorbs
test_eq(a + None, a)
```

``` python
test_eq(repr(b), 'total=5|in=3|out=2|turns=1')
test_eq(repr(UsageStats(total_tokens=9, cost=0.25, cached_tokens=4)),
        'total=9|in=0|out=0|turns=0|cached=4|cost=$0.2500')
test_eq(UsageStats().fmt(), '')
```

## Callbacks

A callback is an object with methods that run at fixed points in a chat
turn. The method `before_send` runs just before the message is sent. The
method `after_response` runs just after the reply arrives. Urai uses
callbacks to add behavior to a turn without a change to the backend.
Counting tokens, recording history, and reminding the model about its
tools are all callbacks.

To write a callback, subclass
[`ChatCallback`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#chatcallback)
and define a method named after the event. The callback reads any
attribute it does not define from the chat it is attached to. In the
method, `self.turn_res` is the current reply of the chat. The attribute
`order` sets which callback runs first. The callback with the lowest
`order` runs first. Setting `run=False` turns a callback off and keeps
it attached.

`run_cbs(chat, event)` runs one event on every callback of a chat. A
callback method can `yield` values.
[`run_cbs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#run_cbs) passes
them to its caller. A callback uses this to add text to a streamed
reply. In the example below, `Quiet` has the lower `order` and runs
first:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/core.py#L73"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### run_cbs

``` python
def run_cbs(
    chat, event
):
```

*Run `event` on each enabled callback of `chat` in `order`, yielding
whatever the callbacks yield.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/core.py#L68"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### ChatCallback

``` python
def ChatCallback(
    *args, **kwargs
):
```

*Base class for chat callbacks. A callback reads attributes it lacks
from the chat, for example `self.turn_msg`.*

``` python
class TinyChat: pass
class Loud(ChatCallback):
    order = 1
    def after_response(self): yield f'loud saw {self.turn_res}'
class Quiet(ChatCallback):
    order = 0
    def after_response(self): yield 'quiet first'
c = TinyChat(); c.turn_res = 'hi'; c.cbs = L(Loud(), Quiet())
for cb in c.cbs: cb.chat = c
test_eq(list(run_cbs(c, 'after_response')), ['quiet first', 'loud saw hi'])
test_eq(list(run_cbs(c, 'before_send')), [])   # no callback defines it
```

``` python
c.cbs[0].run = False
test_eq(list(run_cbs(c, 'after_response')), ['quiet first'])
test_eq(repr(Quiet()), 'Quiet')
```

## Reading a reply

A reply is a plain dict in the OpenAI chat format. Its `content` is a
string or a list of typed parts. A typed part is a dict such as
`{'type': 'text', 'text': ...}`. A tool call is a request from the model
to run one of your functions. A tool call is also a typed part. Backends
produce both forms of `content`. Do not index into `content` to get the
words of a reply.

[`resp_text`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#resp_text)
returns the text of a reply in either form. It joins the text parts and
skips the other parts. It returns an empty string for anything that is
not a dict.
[`thought`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#thought)
returns what a reasoning model wrote before it answered. Urai keeps this
text under `channels['thought']`.
[`truncated`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#truncated)
returns `True` when the reply was cut off at the output token limit.
[`has_tool_call`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#has_tool_call)
returns `True` when a streamed chunk holds a tool call.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/core.py#L95"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
test_eq(resp_text({'content': 'plain'}), 'plain')
test_eq(resp_text({'content': [{'type':'text','text':'a'}, {'type':'tool_call','name':'f'},
                               {'type':'text','text':'b'}]}), 'ab')
test_eq(resp_text(None), '')
test_eq(thought({'channels': {'thought': 'hmm'}}), 'hmm')
test_eq(thought({}), '')
test_eq(truncated({'truncated': True}), True)
test_eq(has_tool_call({'content': [{'type':'tool_call','name':'f'}]}), True)
test_eq(has_tool_call({'content': 'text only'}), False)
```

## Rendering

[`Resp`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#resp) is a dict
subclass that displays itself as markdown in a notebook. The display has
four parts, in this order. The first part is the thinking of the model,
as a quoted block. The second part is the answer text. The third part is
one line for each tool call. The fourth part is one line for each tool
result. Backends return
[`Resp`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#resp) objects. A
reply shows formatted when you evaluate it in a notebook cell.

Three helpers format the parts.
[`quote_`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#quote_) makes a
thinking block, and
[`Resp`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#resp) uses it.
[`tc_summary_`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#tc_summary_)
makes a one-line summary of a tool call, and the stream formatter below
uses it.
[`mk_tr_details`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#mk_tr_details)
makes a collapsible block that holds the arguments and the result of a
tool call as JSON. No other code in the `urai` package calls
[`mk_tr_details`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#mk_tr_details).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/core.py#L117"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
test_eq(quote_('one\ntwo'), '> **🧠 Thinking**\n>\n> one\n> two')
test_eq(tc_summary_('add', {'a': 1}), '<code>add(a=1)</code>')
test_eq(tc_summary_('esc', {'s': '<b>'}), '<code>esc(s=&#x27;&lt;b&gt;&#x27;)</code>')  # escaped for html
assert '```json' in mk_tr_details('add', {'a': 1}, 3)
```

``` python
test_eq(Resp({'content': 'hi'})._repr_markdown_(), 'hi')
test_eq(Resp({})._repr_markdown_(), '*(no text)*')
r = Resp({'content': 'done', 'channels': {'thought': 'why'},
          'tool_calls': [{'function': {'name': 'add', 'arguments': {'a': 1}}}]})
md = r._repr_markdown_()
assert md.startswith('> **🧠 Thinking**') and 'done' in md and '🔧 add' in md
```

## Streaming

A streamed reply arrives as many small chunk dicts. Each chunk holds a
few tokens of thinking or answer text.
[`StreamFormatter`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#streamformatter)
turns the chunks into markdown that you can print or display as it
arrives. It opens a quoted thinking block at the first thinking chunk
and adds to the block as more thinking arrives. It closes the block when
the answer text starts or the stream ends. `showthink=False` hides
thinking. `showcalls=True` adds a line for each tool call.

[`display_stream`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#display_stream)
takes the markdown chunks that a streaming chat produces. It shows them
in one notebook output that updates in place. It returns the full
markdown.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/core.py#L158"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### StreamFormatter

``` python
def StreamFormatter(
    mx:int=2000, showthink:bool=True, showcalls:bool=False
):
```

*Format a chunk stream to markdown. Thinking streams as one blockquote.*

``` python
chunks = [{'channels': {'thought': 'let me'}}, {'channels': {'thought': ' see'}},
          {'content': 'the answer'}]
test_eq(''.join(StreamFormatter().format_stream(chunks)),
        '> **🧠 Thinking**\n>\n> let me see\n\nthe answer')
```

``` python
f = StreamFormatter()
test_eq(''.join(f.format_stream([{'channels': {'thought': 'just thinking'}}])),
        '> **🧠 Thinking**\n>\n> just thinking\n\n')   # closed at the end of the stream
test_eq(f.outp, '> **🧠 Thinking**\n>\n> just thinking')  # ...but the close is not part of the text
test_eq(''.join(StreamFormatter(showthink=False).format_stream(chunks)), 'the answer')
```

``` python
call = [{'content': [{'type': 'tool_call', 'name': 'add', 'arguments': {'a': 1}}]}]
test_eq(''.join(StreamFormatter(showcalls=True).format_stream(call)),
        '\n- ⏳ <code>add(a=1)</code>\n')
test_eq(''.join(StreamFormatter().format_stream(call)), '')   # calls are hidden by default
```

## Stock callbacks

This page defines two stock pieces that need nothing from the tool loop.
The callbacks that need the tool loop are in [loop](loop.html).

`tool_reminder_` is the text that
[`ToolReminderCallback`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/loop.html#toolremindercallback)
adds to a message when the chat has tools. The text asks the model to
summarize each tool result in prose before it continues.
`TruncationCallback(max_tokens)` marks the reply as truncated when the
completion tokens of the turn reach `max_tokens`. Use it with a backend
that reports usage but does not report when it stops at the limit.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/core.py#L171"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### TruncationCallback

``` python
def TruncationCallback(
    max_tokens
):
```

*Flag a reply that reaches the output cap when usage data is available.*

``` python
c = TinyChat(); c.use = UsageStats(completion_tokens=100); c.turn_res = Resp({'content': 'cut off'})
c.cbs = L(TruncationCallback(max_tokens=100)); c.cbs[0].chat = c
list(run_cbs(c, 'after_response'))
test_eq(truncated(c.turn_res), True)
```

``` python
c.use = UsageStats(completion_tokens=99); c.turn_res = Resp({'content': 'room to spare'})
list(run_cbs(c, 'after_response'))
test_eq(truncated(c.turn_res), False)
```
